title: Delegate
markdown:
**What it is:** The place where you decide what the Executive may do without asking you. **Delegate** is in the main menu. It has three tabs: **Act as me**, **Handle it for me** and **Take the lead**. Clicking **Delegate** opens **Act as me**. **What it does for you** sits beside each tab.

**What it does:**

- **What it does for you** says what the Executive does with your settings right now: what it sends on its own, what asks first and what it writes for you to send. It only reads. Nothing on it changes a setting.
- **Act as me** lets the Executive write email drafts *as you*, from your own Gmail or Outlook mailbox. You send them. It can also write first replies to mail in your inbox that needs you.
- **Handle it for me** lets it send some of those replies, and some follow-ups, on its own from your mailbox.
- **Take the lead** (the owner only) lets the Executive act in its own name on what it finds, without waiting to be asked.
- Normally the Executive writes only as itself, from its own email account. Nothing goes out as you unless you set it up here.

**How to use:**

1. Click **Delegate** in the sidebar. (On a phone, open the menu with the button at the top left.)
2. Read **What it does for you**, beside the tab, to see what goes out on its own today.
3. Open **Act as me**, connect your mailbox, and pick what it writes as you.
4. If you want replies sent for you, open **Handle it for me** and pick how much it sends on its own.
5. If you are the owner, open **Take the lead** to let the Executive act in its own name.

**What it does for you:**

- On a wide screen it sits to the right of each Delegate tab. Close it with **✕**, and **What it does** at the top of the tab brings it back; this browser remembers which. On a narrow screen, tap **What it does** at the top of the tab and it opens as a sheet from the bottom.
- Change a setting on the tab and it updates at once. The rows that changed are marked **Just changed** for a few seconds.
- Three pills: **As you**, **Executive** and **Departments**. The number on each pill is how many things go out on their own.
- **As you** covers your own mailbox: emails you ask for in chat, inbox replies, what Handle it for me sends, what is in training, what it has learned and your own rules.
- **Executive** covers what the Executive does in its own name: Take the lead, its Always asks first switches, the company's rules and meetings. Only the owner sees this pill.
- **Departments** shows each department's authority level and what that level covers.
- Rows are grouped: **Sends on its own** (green), **Asks first** (amber), **Writes for you to send** and **Off** (grey). Each row says what it does in one line, then why, with a link to the setting.
- **Compare Act as me, Handle it for me and Take the lead**, at the bottom, opens **Who writes and who sends**. Pick a tab and one of its options. Three answers sit on top: who writes it, whose name is on it and who presses Send. Under them the steps appear one at a time and stay on screen, for example Dana emails you, you ask in chat, the Executive writes the draft, you tap Send. **Handle it for me** shows the same five emails at every level, each marked **Sent as you** or **Waits for you**. Tapping there changes no setting. **Play again** replays the steps.
- While the Executive is paused, a note at the top says nothing runs on its own, with a **Resume** link.
- Someone who is not on the People list sees "Only people on the team can see this."

**Act as me:**

- Who can use it: the owner. Team members can use it once the owner turns on **Let team members use it** (under **Advanced** on this tab). That switch shows only when the install allows it. Anyone else sees "Act as me isn't available to you here."
- Each person connects their own mailbox and turns it on for themselves. What it reads in your mail, the drafts it writes and your reply cards are yours alone. The owner sees only each team member's name, how many drafts they had written and sent in the last 30 days, and whether inbox replies are on. A conversation in which it read someone's mail can be opened only by that person.
- **Your mailbox**: until it is connected, the card shows the command to run on a computer with a browser (one for Gmail and, where the install supports it, one for Outlook). Sign in as yourself, put the file it writes where the API reads it, then click **Check again**. Once connected it shows "Connected to" your address. It won't connect the Executive's own address as yours.
- **What it writes as you**: "Nothing goes out until you send it." Pick one:
  - **Off**: the Executive only writes as itself.
  - **When I ask**: ask in chat, "reply to Dana as me: yes to the 5th", and the draft waits in your Gmail or Outlook Drafts.
  - **Draft replies automatically**: it also writes a first reply to mail that needs you, and puts it on Home.
- You can't move up from **Off** until your mailbox is connected. Moving down asks first, says what stops, and saves when you click **Move down**. Moving to **When I ask** stops inbox replies. Moving to **Off** stops everything it writes as you and turns **Read my calendar** off. Either one also stops Handle it for me if it was sending.
- **Learn from my edits** (a checkbox once you are above **Off**): when you change a draft before sending, tick **Do it like this next time** and it learns how you write to that person. Nothing more is sent.
- **Read my calendar**: a switch. On, it reads your own calendar when you ask about your day or week in chat, and offers your free slots when a reply needs a time. It also brings meeting invites from people you know to Home as cards (see **Meeting invites** below). The only change it makes to your calendar is answering an invite: when you tap **Accept** or **Decline**, or an accept on its own under Handle it for me. It stays off while **What it writes as you** is at **Off**. If your mailbox sign-in doesn't include your calendar, the card shows a command to run once to add it. A sign-in you made before invites could be answered still reads your calendar; run the same command again to let it answer invites.
- **Suggested actions**: meeting invites and messages your mail calls for. **Always ask** brings each one to you as a card, every time. **In training** also brings each one as a card; tick **Do this on its own next time** before **Approve** and it does that kind, with those people, on its own from then on. **On** sends the message or invite on its own, no card; new contacts, anyone added in the last week, money, links and the topics that always wait still come to you, up to 10 a day.
- **What it's learned**: what it learned from your edits (drafts) and your approvals (suggested actions). Each item says when, how many times it has been used since, and an example. **Remove** forgets it, and it asks you again.
- **Advanced** (closed by default) holds **How I write**, **AI line on drafts you send** (shown only when the install adds an AI line to mail) and, for the owner, **Let team members use it**.

**Asking in chat:**

- Ask in the web app (signed in), in a direct message to the Executive on Slack or Discord, or in a private Telegram chat: "reply to Dana as me: yes to the 5th."
- It saves a draft in your own Drafts and shows a card, "Drafted an email as you to Dana — in your Drafts". Asking in chat never sends anything by itself. In the web app the draft also appears under the reply as **Email as you**, with who it goes to, the subject and the start of the text, and a **Send** button: tapping it sends that draft from your mailbox, exactly as it was written. If you changed the draft in your mailbox first, send it from there.
- It does not write as you in a shared channel or thread, on Google Chat, from an email, from a scheduled job or in anyone else's conversation.
- If it isn't sure about something, it asks you instead of guessing.
- There is a daily limit on drafts written as one person (50 a day unless the install changes it).

**Draft replies automatically:**

- About every five minutes it looks at new mail in your inbox. For mail that needs a personal reply from you (a question, a request, a meeting to arrange, an introduction or a follow-up), it writes a first reply and puts it at the top of **Needs you** on Home.
- It only looks at mail that arrives after you turn it on. It leaves out newsletters, notifications, mailing lists, automatic mail, mail you are not in To or Cc on, mail you've already answered and anything that doesn't need you. Mail you answer within ten minutes never gets a draft.
- The first reply only acknowledges. It repeats only what you've already said in the thread, commits you to nothing and lists what's left for you to decide, each with a few short answers to tap. Tap one, or **Something else…** to type your own, and it rewrites the reply with your answer. For a time, with **Read my calendar** on, it offers your next free slots. For a document, it offers one from your documents to say you'll send it (it can't attach files). **Send** waits until you've answered, or until you change the words with **Edit**. Someone you've never written to gets a short holding reply.
- Under the picker you see how it is doing (for example, that your mailbox needs connecting again) and when it last looked. Click **Check now** to look straight away.
- **Also save inbox replies in my Gmail Drafts** (or Outlook): off by default, so replies wait on their cards only. Tick it to keep each reply in your Drafts too.
- On each card on Home: **Send** asks you to confirm who it goes to, then **Send now**. In training, tick **Reply to <name> on its own next time** before **Send** and replies to that person go on their own from then on. **Edit** changes the words on the card. **Open in Gmail** opens it when it is in your Drafts. **Dismiss** removes the card.
- Limits: at most 5 drafts a check and 20 a day unless the install changes it, 2 a day per sender (1 for a stranger), and never more than 25 cards open. A card closes when the draft is sent or deleted in your mailbox, when you reply yourself, or after 7 days.

**Meeting invites (with Read my calendar on):**

- An invite from someone you know (your team, a contact, or someone you've written to) becomes a card in **Needs you** on Home: the meeting, when it is, who invited you and anything on your calendar it clashes with. Only the busy times are shown, never what the other meetings are.
- **Accept** or **Decline** answers it in your own calendar, and your calendar lets them know. **Dismiss** removes the card without answering.
- Invites from people you don't know, from an address your mail service couldn't confirm, meetings that aren't on your calendar, ones you've already answered and ones that have started are left alone, as before.
- If your sign-in can read your calendar but not answer invites, the card says so and shows the command to connect again under **Read my calendar**. Until then, answer it in your calendar.
- A card closes by itself once the meeting starts, or after 7 days.

**How I write (under Advanced):**

- Shows your style as a few sentences, with where it came from ("Learned from N of your sent emails", or "Set by you") and whether it is locked.
- **Describe it in your own words**: write how you write, the way you'd tell a new assistant (up to 2,000 characters). Buttons add common phrases, such as "Short and to the point" or "No emojis". Click **Write my style**; it shows the new style with new lines marked **New** and a sample reply. Click **Save** to keep it or **Change it** to edit your words. Nothing changes until you save.
- **Learn from my sent mail** (or **Learn again from my sent mail**): reads your recent sent emails once and describes how you write. It needs your mailbox connected and is hidden while the style is locked.
- **Fine-tune details** opens the fields: **Length** (short, medium, long), **Tone** (casual, neutral, formal), a **Greeting** **To your team**, **To your contacts** and **To anyone else** ({first} becomes their first name), **Sign-off**, **Habits** and **Never** (one per line), your **Signature** and **Examples of your writing**.
- **Save changes** saves the fields. **Lock** stops it being relearned from your mail (you can still edit it); **Unlock** undoes that. **Reset** starts over. **Remove examples** drops the examples.
- **Signature**: with Gmail, your signature is added to every draft. **Refresh from Gmail** picks up a change you made in Gmail, **Don't add my signature** stops adding it, and **Add my Gmail signature** brings it back. Outlook doesn't share signatures with apps, so Outlook drafts end with your sign-off.
- **AI line on drafts you send**: a checkbox for whether drafts you approve and send end with the install's AI line. Off unless the install starts it on. A change applies to the next reply it writes.

**Handle it for me:**

- It sends from your own mailbox, on its own, some of the replies Act as me writes for your inbox, and some follow-ups. With **Read my calendar** on, it also accepts meeting invites from your team and contacts on its own when nothing on your calendar clashes. It never declines on its own: a clash, or an invite from someone it may not handle, still comes to you as a card.
- It needs **Draft replies automatically** on the Act as me tab. Until then the card says so and offers **Turn on Draft replies automatically**, or **Connect your mailbox in Act as me** if your mailbox isn't connected.
- Someone who can't have Act as me sees that Handle it for me isn't available to them.
- **What it sends on its own**: **Off**, **In training** or **On**.
  - **Off**: every reply waits for you to send.
  - **In training**: every reply, follow-up and invite comes to you first. Tick **Reply to <name> on its own next time** (or **Follow up with them on its own next time**) on a card before **Send** and it handles that person on its own from then on. On an invite card, tick **Accept from <name> on its own next time** before **Accept** and their invites with no clash are accepted on their own from then on.
  - **On**: it sends what the step under **How much it sends** allows:
  - **Easy ones**: only short replies to people you know, when it's very sure. Follow-ups are written for you and wait on Home.
  - **People I know**: replies to people you know. Strangers, links and amounts wait for you. Follow-ups go to your team and contacts when they haven't answered a question of yours in a few days.
  - **Most mail**: also strangers and longer replies, and links or amounts when it's very sure. Follow-ups go to anyone you wrote to who hasn't answered a question of yours in a few days.
  - **Everything** (the owner only): it decides what to send as you. Replies with a link, the topics that always wait and your rules still hold it back.
- **In training** and **On** need signed sign-ins on the server. Without them they are greyed out with "Needs signed sign-ins on this server." Turning it off or moving down a step asks first and saves when you confirm.
- Money, contracts, legal, hiring, the press and passwords always wait for you. It never writes to anyone the email didn't go to. A reply that names the Executive waits too.
- **Your rules** (at **Everything**): replies matching one wait for you, on top of the company's rules. Pick **A person**, **A company**, **Words** or **An amount**, type the value and click **Add rule**. **Remove** deletes one.
- **What it sent** (while it is on): "Sent N replies on its own today", then each reply and follow-up from the last week: who it went to, the subject, **Still yours to answer** for questions it left for you, and **Open in your mailbox**. An invite it accepted shows as one line, for example "Accepted Dana's Pilot review, Wed 21 Oct, 14:30", and counts toward the same daily limit.
- **Who it's allowed to handle**: the people you ticked to handle on their own. **Remove** takes one off, and it asks you again.
- **AI line on replies it sends** (under **Advanced**, when the install adds an AI line): on by default. Turning it off asks you to confirm with **Turn it off** or **Keep it on**.
- Limits: 20 replies sent on its own a day unless the install changes it, and one a conversation. Past the limit, replies wait on cards.

**Take the lead:**

- The owner's alone. Anyone else sees "Only the account owner can turn this on."
- **Off**: when it looks over your day, it tells you what it would do, and you do it.
- **In training**: everything it would do comes to you as a card on Home first. What you allow, it does on its own from then on.
- **On**: it acts on what it finds while it looks over your day: it messages people, books meetings and starts workflows. Anything under **Always asks first** waits for a yes.
- **In training** and **On** need signed sign-ins on the server.
- **What it's learned**: the actions you ticked **on its own next time** on a card. **Remove** takes one off. Something you approved unchanged three times shows as a suggestion with **Allow**.
- **Always asks first**: a switch for each: **Money**, **Contracts and legal**, **Hiring and people decisions**, **Deleting, cancelling or sharing**, **Someone new** and **Big sends** (company-wide or department-wide, or more than five people). These wait for you, or for whoever approves that area, with a card on Home. **Meetings asked for in chat** is the last row: meetings you or a teammate ask it to book (in a team, Operations must also act on its own). A meeting it thinks of itself always waits. While Take the lead is off, only the meetings row applies.
- Department levels don't hold what it does here. The switches and rules do.
- **Company rules**: anything matching one always waits for a yes, for the Executive and for everyone's sending as themselves. Add them the same way as **Your rules**.
- **Pause** on **Settings → Your Executive** stops everything on this tab. Anything you tap **Send** or **Approve** on still goes.

**Example prompts:**

- "Reply to Dana as me: yes to the 5th, and ask her to send the deck first."
- "Write to the Acme team as me and push our call to Thursday."
- "What's on my calendar tomorrow?" (with **Read my calendar** on)
